title: Why my mom stays home on Friday the 13th
author: Storytime
hook: My mom has never left the house on a Friday the thirteenth. Today, she finally told me why.
story: My whole life, every Friday the thirteenth, my mom stays home. She takes the day off work. She doesn't drive. She doesn't even check the mail. We all thought she was just superstitious. This morning, she called me at seven. She sounded panicked. She said, can you come over? I need to tell you something before your father wakes up. When I got there, she was sitting at the kitchen table with her phone. She said, thirty-one years ago, on a Friday the thirteenth, I went to Las Vegas with my friends. I was twenty-two. I met a man at a casino. We had too much champagne. And we got married. In a chapel. By a guy dressed as a cowboy. She flew home the next day and never saw him again. She thought it was never official. She married my dad two years later. Last night, she got a message from a man named Gary. He's sixty. He's getting remarried. And his lawyer just found out he's still legally married. To my mom. Which means my parents' marriage might not be legal. And my dad is upstairs, still asleep. Part two?
caption: it wasn't superstition. it was Gary 🎰 #storytime
sound: a spooky, comedic suspense theme at very low volume
why: Posted on Friday the 13th, the superstition hook is timely, the Vegas chapel twist is absurd and shareable, and the sleeping dad sets up a strong part two.

title: Dropped from the bridal party
author: Storytime
hook: My best friend dropped me from her bridal party because I couldn't afford her bachelorette trip. Then she found out where she booked it.
story: My best friend Jade is getting married in the spring. In September, she sent the bridesmaids a message. The bachelorette trip is mandatory. Five nights at a luxury resort in Cabo. Fifteen hundred dollars each, due in two weeks. I'd just lost my job. I told her honestly that I couldn't make it work, but I'd love to help plan something smaller. She replied, if you can't show up for me, you're not really a bridesmaid. And she removed me from the group chat. Here's the thing Jade never asked about. My family owns that resort. My aunt manages it. I spent every summer there as a kid. Last week, my aunt called me laughing. She said, a bride named Jade just tried to negotiate a group discount. She mentioned she used to have a best friend with the same last name as us. Then she said something that made my aunt go quiet. She said, but she's poor now, so we don't talk. My aunt asked me what I wanted her to do. Upgrade them? Charge full price? Mention my name at check-in? Jade lands in three weeks. What should I tell my aunt?
caption: she should have read the resort website 🌴 #storytime
sound: a breezy tropical beat with a sly twist at very low volume
why: Bachelorette cost drama is a proven viral genre, the never asked line sets up the reveal, the resort owner twist is satisfying karma, and asking viewers what to do drives comments.

title: Sister in law said just bring ice
author: Storytime
hook: Every Thanksgiving, my sister-in-law assigns everyone a dish. For five years, mine has been just bring ice.
story: My wife's sister, Karen, hosts Thanksgiving every year. And every year, she sends a group text assigning everyone a dish. Her mom gets the turkey. Her husband gets the pie. My wife gets the sides. And me? Just bring ice. Five years in a row. She thinks it's funny. She once told the whole table, he's not really a kitchen guy. Here's what Karen doesn't know. I'm a pastry chef. I've worked in restaurant kitchens for twelve years. My wife just never mentioned it, because Karen never asked what I do. This year the text came in. Just bring ice, lol. My wife looked at me and said, do it. So I did. I spent three nights at the restaurant after closing. On Thanksgiving, I walked in carrying a cooler. Inside was a sculpture made of ice. A turkey. Life size. With a hollow center filled with a chocolate mousse I'd made from scratch. Karen's kids screamed. Her mom cried. Her husband asked for my number. And Karen just stood there and said, you could have told us. I said, you could have asked. Now she wants me to make the dessert next year. Should I say yes, or keep bringing ice?
caption: I brought ice. technically 🧊 #storytime
sound: a triumphant, cheeky orchestral beat at very low volume
why: Thanksgiving dish assignments are relatable family friction, the not a kitchen guy line sets up the reveal, the ice sculpture is a visual payoff, and the final question invites petty answers.
